segments.t: If you have a temperament that when others are fearful, you're going to get scared yourself.
You know, you are not going to make a lot of money in securities over time in all probability.
That, you know, people really, if they didn't look at quotations, but of course the whole
world is urging them to look at quotations, and more than that do something based on
small changes in quotations, but if you didn't, think how much more rational, we've talked
about it before, but think how much more rational investing in a farm is than the
way many people buy stocks. If you buy a farm, do you get a quote next week? Do you get a
quote next month? If you buy an apartment house, do you get a quote next week or month?
No, you look at the apartment house or the farm and you say, I expected it to produce
so many bushels of soybeans and corn, and if it does that, it meets my expectations.
But they buy a stock and they think if it goes up, it's wonderful, and if it goes down, it's bad.
We think just the opposite. When it goes down, we love it because we'll buy more,
and if it goes up, it kills us to buy more. Ben Graham wrote about it, it's been explained,
but if you can't get yourself in that mental attitude, you're going to be scared
whenever everybody else is scared, and expect somebody else to tell you when to buy and
therefore get your courage back up or something. I could get this fellow's courage up
substantially by saying it's a wonderful time to buy, and then a week from now,
you'd run into somebody else that tells them the world is coming to an end, and they'd sell.
I mean, he's a broker's friend.
